title: L3 Quarter-Review: Error-Proof Your Code
story: Congratulations! You've learned Option, Result, match, and `?` — XIOM's complete toolkit for crash-free code. Now it's time for the final exam: a mini-program that combines everything. Your code will be bulletproof — no crash, no mystery, just clear handling of every case.
why: This review ties together every L3 concept into a single working program — parsing, validation, transformation, error propagation, and pattern matching all working in concert.
analogy: This final program is like a quality control station — every part that comes through gets inspected, measured, and either approved with a green stamp (Ok) or rejected with a detailed note (Err). Nothing slips through.
try_it: Add two more configs: "cache_size" (range 1-1024) and "log_level" (range 0-5). Need all 5 to pass? Modify the program to print 'ALL SYSTEMS GO' only if every config passed. If any failed, print 'CONFIG ERROR — check settings.'
tips: The `?` operator is your best friend — it collapses parse + check + return into one line
Match is for when you need different logic per case; .unwrap_or is for simple defaults
Always consider: could this fail? If yes, return Result. Could this be missing? If yes, return Option
common_mistakes: Using .unwrap_or too early in a pipeline — it discards the error; keep Result until the final handler
Writing match arms that don't actually handle the error — `Err(e) => {}` silently ignores problems
Counting failures by nesting if-else inside match — use separate match statements or counters in arms
